term: director regress, cognition and understanding (formal interface)
definition: A director is a being related by Directs to a thing and an end. The regress reuses the first-way MovesIn/MovedIn relations and its strong per-se link: a mover distinct from its effect that itself moves in any respect is linked by MovesAsMoved, with the advertised no-infinite-series premise. A director moved by none is moved in no respect. HasCognition and Intelligent are distinct primitive predicates for knowing and understanding; they are not inferred just by calling something a director. DirectionPassesToMoversOfDirectors and UnmovedDirectorKnowsAndUnderstands are separate open bridges, not definitions of motion or conclusions already supplied by q.103.
note: Exposes the typed vocabulary used by the existing director-regress proof. A sourced account of instrumental dependence and the inference from an unmoved director to knowing/understanding would be needed to discharge the two open bridges. No identification with the skeleton HasIntellect predicate is imposed here.
